definitions.explanation: The state of being thoroughly wet, typically from rain or water. Used as a noun or as a na-adjective with の.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}でびしょ{濡|ぬ}れになった。
examples.english: I got soaking wet from the rain.

examples.japanese: びしょ{濡|ぬ}れの{服|ふく}を{着替|きが}えた。
examples.english: I changed out of my soaking wet clothes.

examples.japanese: {傘|かさ}を{忘|わす}れて{帰|かえ}ったので、{家|いえ}に{着|つ}いたときにはびしょ{濡|ぬ}れだった。
examples.english: I forgot my umbrella on the way home, so by the time I got home I was drenched.

notes:
FORMATION:
びしょ is an intensifying prefix meaning "thoroughly" or "completely." Combined with {濡|ぬ}れ (wetness), it describes being completely soaked.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- びしょ{濡|ぬ}れになる (to get soaking wet)
- びしょ{濡|ぬ}れの{服|ふく} (soaking wet clothes)
- {雨|あめ}でびしょ{濡|ぬ}れ (drenched from rain)

RELATED WORDS:
- ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れ: soaking wet — similar meaning, slightly stronger emphasis
